body:
Additional finding while working #10221: fixing only the bash-version symptom is not enough on macOS.

I compiled bash 5.2 into an isolated prefix (not touching `/opt/homebrew`, no sudo) and re-ran `os-verify-lock.sh -c '...'` through it — `mapfile`/`EPOCHSECONDS` both work now, confirmed with a standalone smoke test. The acquisition still failed: `VERDICT queue-timeout (exit 99) · never acquired · waited 540s · never reached the head of the queue · lock is free` — genuinely uncontended (`/tmp/os-heavy-verify.lock.q` empty, no `.holder` file), yet my own ticket never reached the head.

Root cause is a second, independent macOS gap: `ticket_alive()` (`scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh:172-180`) gates every ticket — including the caller's own — on `[[ -d "/proc/${pid}" ]]` and a `/proc/<pid>/stat` read via `proc_starttime()`. macOS has no `/proc` filesystem at all, so `ticket_alive` returns false unconditionally, `queue_live` prunes every ticket (including a solo, uncontested one) on the very next scan, and the ordering loop can never find `TICKET` in the live set — hence an unconditional queue-timeout regardless of contention. Separately, `lock_is_held()`/the actual acquisition call on `flock` (used for `--status`'s definitive check and presumably the real acquire path) has no macOS target either — this host has no `flock` binary (`brew`'s util-linux isn't installed).

So fix-shape option 1 in this issue ("portable equivalents" for `mapfile`/`EPOCHSECONDS`) would still leave the wrapper permanently non-functional on macOS — the ticket-liveness and holder-detection logic need a `/proc`-free (e.g. `ps -p <pid> -o lstart=`/`ps -o etime=`) and `flock`-free (e.g. `mkdir`-based or `shlock`) path too. Not attempting that fix here — out of scope for #10221 — but noting it so option 1's estimate accounts for it before someone picks it up.

Worked around the same way #10219 did: ran #10221's verification directly (`pnpm --filter ...`), without the lock, declared in the PR body.

⭐ Priority note from the dispatching seat: this is not a broken helper, it is the **single entry point every dev agent is instructed to route every build and test through**. Three of tonight's four dev reports quote `os-verify-lock` VERDICT lines, so the blast radius is every dispatch on a macOS host. The unbounded-retry shape is the sharp end: no acquisition budget is exceeded, so nothing times out, no `VERDICT` line is ever printed, and the spinning waiters compete for CPU with the real build the lock exists to protect.

⛔ Governed surface out of scope for the diff (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `content/docs/releases/**`) — propose wording in the report instead.
⭐ Changeset: this lane's dispatch template was wrong about this and is now fixed. `AGENTS.md:943` — *"Pure bug fixes do not require a changeset"*. For a `scripts/**`-only diff that publishes nothing, the repo's own gate prescribes the **`skip-changeset` label** (applied via the additive `POST /labels`, never a whole-set PUT); `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` rejects the empty-frontmatter route. Precedent: PR #10502, merged 2026-08-21.
